name: Brian Abbott Fish Barrier Removal Board grants

funder.name: Washington Recreation and Conservation Office (Brian Abbott Fish Barrier Removal Board)

summary: Washington State grants to design and build fixes for fish passage barriers such as culverts, small dams and logjams, open to nonprofits, tribes, landowners, fisheries enhancement groups and public bodies.

steps: Application refinement and final PRISM submission

eligibility.rule: The project has no 0% passable downstream barriers
The project is not an injunction culvert or mitigation requirement
The project has no federal structures
The project results in full passage for salmon and/or steelhead
Linear gain is greater than zero
The project has a Qualitative Habitat Assessment value of at least 300
A planning project results in final project design
Not property acquisition, capital public works, or grant application costs

co_finance.applies_to: Planning grants over $500,000 and restoration grants over $750,000

documents: Landowner Acknowledgement Form, for land the applicant does not own
Landowner support documentation, for land the sponsor does not own
Vicinity map and detailed site map
Photos of the barrier and upstream habitat
Preliminary designs, if requesting $500,000 or more for a restoration project

applicant_types.quote: Local agencies Native American tribes Nonprofit organizations Private landowners Regional fisheries enhancement organizations Special purpose districts such as port, park and recreation, conservation, and school districts State agencies

geography.quote: barriers to fish passage on Washington's waterways are removed

window.quote: Funding is awarded every two years and comes from the sale of bonds.

effort.quote: Complete and submit the PRISM Online application and attachments by January 26th
Work with WDFW biologists for onsite barrier evaluation (if needed)
Re-submit your updated, final application by May 7th

eligibility.quote: Not an injunction culvert or mitigation requirement
Result in full passage for salmon and/or steelhead
Linear gain must be greater than zero
Minimum Qualitative Habitat Assessment value of 300
Planning (design-only) must result in final project design.

Acquisition of property through full fee interest or permanent easement Capital facilities and public works projects, such as sewer treatment facilities, surface and storm water management systems, and water supply systems Costs to apply for a Brian Abbott Fish Barrier Removal Board grant

co_finance.quote: Planning grants exceeding $500,000 15 percent and grants may exceed two years Restoration (construction) grants less than or equal to $750,000 None Restoration (construction) grants exceeding $750,000 15 percent of the grant total

documents.quote: Cost Estimate. RCO recommends using its template or similar format.
Landowner Acknowledgement Form is required for projects on land not owned by the applicant
Landowner project support documentation for projects occurring on non-sponsor owned property (email, letter, etc.)
General vicinity map for all projects • One large-scale, detailed map showing the site clearly marked and labeled with road names, and correctly mapped streams
One photo of the barrier, preferably of outlet (downstream end) if safe to acquire • One photo of the upstream habitat
Barrier Evaluation Forms. Completed Barrier Evaluation Forms may be available on WDFW
For restoration projects requesting $500,000 or more, preliminary designs must be submitted with the application package.
Lead Entity Letter of Support: confirms that the project supports the recovery plan or is on the Planned Project Forecast List if project is not specifically identified in either document.
Applicant Resolution and Authorization is required for any sponsor who will sign the grant agreement.

after_award.quote: A minimum of two progress reports are required each year.
Ten percent of project costs will be retained until RCO completes a final inspection.
